cards.text: Paul is writing to the believers in Rome (Romans 1:7). He just said God did not reject His people Israel (Romans 11:2), a remnant was chosen by grace (Romans 11:5), and the others were hardened (Romans 11:7). Now Paul asks the big one: did they stumble so as to fall beyond recovery?

cards.question: Paul says Israel stumbled so badly that they fell beyond recovery.

cards.text: Paul's answer: “Certainly not!” ZERO wiggle room, friend, but because of Israel's trespass, something has come to the Gentiles, the nations who aren't Israel.

cards.question: Because of Israel's trespass, what has come to the Gentiles?
Paul says salvation has come to the Gentiles to make Israel ___.

cards.text: Watch Paul now, baker. This man is about to do MATH: if Israel's trespass means riches for the world, and their failure means riches for the Gentiles, then what?

cards.question: What does Paul say Israel's fullness will bring?

cards.text: Then Paul talks straight to the Gentiles. He's the apostle to the Gentiles, and he magnifies his ministry, hoping to provoke his own people to jealousy.

cards.question: Paul hopes to provoke his own people to jealousy and ___ some of them.

cards.text: And Paul will NOT sit down. If their rejection is the reconciliation of the world, he asks, what will their acceptance be?

cards.question: Paul asks what Israel's acceptance will be. What does he call it?

cards.text: Then Paul pulls out a picture, and baker, it's DOUGH. Years I sat on a kitchen counter, and FINALLY a letter in the Bible talks my language.

cards.question: Paul says if the first part of the dough is holy, so is the ___ batch.
Right after the dough, Paul gives a tree picture: if the root is holy, the branches are not.

cards.text: Paul stays with that tree and talks to the Gentiles. If some branches have been broken off, and you, a wild olive shoot, have been grafted in among the others to share the olive root's nourishment, Paul has something to tell you.

cards.question: What does Paul tell the wild olive shoot not to do over the broken-off branches?
Paul reminds the grafted-in wild shoot that it supports the root.

cards.text: Paul even hears the comeback before it's said: “Branches were broken off so that I could be grafted in.” Paul agrees that's correct, and then he keeps talking, and friend, when somebody agrees with you and KEEPS talking, brace yourself.

cards.question: Paul says the natural branches were broken off because of ___, but you stand by ___.

cards.text: Then Paul says, “Do not be arrogant, but be afraid.” And he gives a reason.

cards.question: Paul says that if God did not spare the natural branches, He will surely spare the grafted-in ones.

cards.text: So Paul says take notice. There are two sides of God to see here, like flipping a cookie over, friend: you've got to check BOTH.

cards.question: Branches broken off, a wild shoot grafted in. Which two things about God does Paul tell the Gentiles to notice?
Paul says God shows severity to those who fell. What condition does he give the grafted-in Gentiles?

cards.text: Then Paul adds a warning, and he doesn't soften it one bit: “Otherwise you also will be cut off.”
Now Paul turns back to the branches that got broken off. Baker, a stamper who spent years in the back of a junk drawer is leaning WAY in for this part.

cards.question: Paul says the broken-off branches can never be grafted back in, even if they do not persist in unbelief.

cards.text: Paul gives the reason: God is able to graft them in again. Then his last move: the Gentiles were cut from a wild olive tree and grafted into a cultivated one, contrary to nature, so think about the branches that grew there first.

cards.question: A wild shoot was grafted into a cultivated olive tree, contrary to nature. What does Paul say about the natural branches?

answers.text: They'll be grafted in more readily
They'll be grafted in more slowly
They'll need a different olive tree

findings.problem: Paul shows up for the first time and the card never says who he is. It only says he is writing to the believers in Rome. The baker doesn't learn he's an apostle until stop 1, card 8.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The card spends words defining a hard word ("the Gentiles, the nations who aren't Israel"). The dictionary pop-up should cover "Gentiles".

rule.text: Don't spend card words explaining a hard word. Hard words get a dictionary pop-up (definitions.md, made after the cards).

findings.problem: No earlier card hints at the idea of jealousy, so "jealous" can only be guessed by luck over "afraid" or "ashamed". The blank finishes the wording of verse 11 instead of testing meaning the baker can reason out. Stop 1 already has several discovery questions (cards 4, 11 and 13).

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to finish the wording of the line ("so is the ___ batch"). The setup on card 12 only says the picture is dough, so "whole", "next" and "other" are just guesses at the next word, not meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The setup compares Papa Dorin's years in the junk drawer, where he was forgotten and then found, to the broken-off branches. That signals they can come back, which rules out "True" on the next card (card 13) before the baker answers.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Verse 24 says "For if you were cut from a wild olive tree," but the card turns it into a plain statement ("the Gentiles were cut from a wild olive tree and grafted into a cultivated one"), dropping the "if".
The question states "A wild shoot was grafted into a cultivated olive tree, contrary to nature" as plain fact. It drops the "if" from verse 24.
